# DayPlay

> DayPlay is an ADHD friendly alarm and routine app for iPhone. Its alarm rings
> through Silent mode and Focus, and with "mission lock" it does not stop until
> the user confirms the first step of their routine.

## Facts
- Platform: iOS 15.0 and later. The real system alarm requires iOS 26 or later
  (Apple AlarmKit); on iOS 18 and earlier DayPlay falls back to a burst of
  notifications and says so in the interface.
- Mission lock: pressing the alarm's stop button opens the app on step one of
  the routine; the alarm keeps ringing in app until that step is confirmed.
- Escape protection: while the mission is locked, a backup system alarm is
  kept about 30 seconds ahead and pulled to about 3 seconds when the app is
  left.
- Snoozes are counted per routine (0 to 3). When the budget is spent, the snooze
  button is not rendered.
- Offline first: no account, no DayPlay server. Routines, step names and history
  never leave the device.
- Usage counters (Mixpanel, EU servers) and crash reports (Firebase
  Crashlytics) can be turned off in Settings > Privacy. Routine and step names
  are never sent.
- Pricing: free with up to two routines. DayPlay Pro is $6.99/month or
  $39.99/year with a 7 day free trial, and removes the
  routine limit, adds timing suggestions, a 30-day comparison, extra theme
  packs and flexible streak protection.
- Languages: English and Turkish.
- DayPlay is not a medical device and does not diagnose or treat ADHD.
